title.en: Practical 12: Models of the human heart and brain

text.en: Look inside a model heart and brain and label what you see.

The aim is to observe and draw labelled sketches of the longitudinal section of the human heart and brain from models.
The heart has four chambers: two auricles and two ventricles separated by septa which prevent mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. The tricuspid valve lies between the right auricle and ventricle and the bicuspid valve between the left auricle and ventricle. The heart is covered by the pericardium.
The brain lies in the cranial cavity and controls the body. It is covered by three meninges (dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater) and has forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain.
